summary: Quarterly customer success check-in focused on operational playbook and a forward-looking cost forecast. Agreed on benchmarking next week and exchange of SOC 2/security artifacts. Action items assigned for cost CSV, benchmark plan, and SOW draft.
topics: Latency and p95 reliability during spikes
Optimization levers: batching, KV cache, quantization
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining. We're gonna run about an hour, QBR style — focus on ops playbook and cost forecast. Quick intros?
[00:16] Hannah (Longview): Hi all, Hannah here, heads up MLOps at Longview. Marcus, Priya, Derek are with me.
[00:23] Marcus (Longview): Morning — VP Eng Marcus.
[00:26] Priya (Longview): Priya, cloud architect.
[00:28] Derek (Longview): Derek, SRE.
[00:30] Raj (Redwood SE): Raj — I'll jump into bench and architecture bits.
[00:34] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: current usage and cost drivers, reliability highlights last quarter, recommended playbook for Dedicated pilot, and next steps.
[01:05] Hannah: We've been seeing steady uptick — about 3x in inference calls quarter-over-quarter, mostly chat completions for our customer support product. Costs spiking in Europe region, we think because of long context windows for transcripts.
[01:22] Marcus: Yep, and finance flagged the month-on-month token bill. We're trying to model what a Dedicated pool would do to both lower unit cost and guarantee throughput.
[01:35] Raj: Quick clarifying q — what's your 95th percentile token length and typical session counts? If you can, share a histogram. That shapes batching and kernel selection.
[01:48] Priya: We have a mixed shape — median 150 tokens, p95 around 520, bursts hitting 1k occasionally when agent transcripts are long. We'll send a sample.
[02:12] Raj: Cool — that p95 is large enough that attention memory and KV cache behavior matters. On hosted side, caching prefixes helps but if users send unique long context all the time, batching wins are limited.
[02:30] Hannah: Can you explain batching wins vs KV cache? We've heard both but not sure when each helps.
[02:36] Raj: Sure — batching groups concurrent requests to amortize GPU throughput; best when you have a steady arrival rate and similar sequence lengths. KV cache (prefix caching) reuses cached key-value pairs when requests share earlier tokens — great for short variations on the same prompt. In your use, because transcripts differ a lot, batching + dynamic autoscale gives better unit cost than cache alone.
[03:12] Derek: Are there risks to batching on latency? Our SLA is p95 under 350ms for routing decisions.
[03:20] Raj: Yes, batching adds headroom latency depending on batch window. Redwood's runtime supports latency SLO buckets and small batch windows for p95-sensitive routes. You can also route critical traffic to a smaller Dedicated pool with stricter SLO.
[03:38] Priya: So Dedicated pool gives lower cost but also predictable throughput?
[03:42] Maya: Exactly. Dedicated means reserved GPU capacity, configurable autoscale policies and burst options. Hosted is elastic but price-per-token can be higher and you get multi-tenant variability.
[04:05] Marcus: On cost modeling: what levers do we have — quantization, smaller models, caching, batching? Which are easiest and what's the expected delta?
[04:15] Raj: Short answer: batching + quantization often gives the biggest delta quickly. Example: 4-bit quantization on compatible models can reduce memory and increase throughput — say 25-45% cost drop depending on latency tradeoffs. Batching improvements depend on traffic shape; caching helps if prompt reuse is high. Also model selection: a 7B quantized model vs a 13B float model often hits big wins for NLU tasks.
[05:02] Hannah: Are there output-quality tradeoffs with 4-bit quant? We can't degrade customer experience.
[05:08] Raj: We recommend running small evals using your prompt sets; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per workload. It flags regressions against evals. If you keep a holdback, you can A/B test.
[05:30] Priya: Security — finance also wants to know about data residency, KMS, and audit logs. We run in a locked-down org and require SAML SSO and RBAC.
[05:40] Maya: We heard that — Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem deployments, customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. For Hosted, we provide SOC 2 attestations, encryption at rest/in transit, and per-token logging redaction options. We'll share the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts after the call.
[06:05] Derek: What about log retention and ability to pull raw request traces for forensics?
[06:12] Elena (Redwood CSM): We can export audit logs to your SIEM, retention configurable as an add-on. For the pilot, we'll include a sample export.
[06:23] Hannah: Great. On operational playbook — if we run a Dedicated pilot, what are the recommended guardrails?
[06:30] Raj: Short list: 1) Define per-route SLOs (p95 latency, error budget), 2) Traffic shaping: send critical routes to low-latency pool, 3) Autoscale rules tuned for burst behavior (scale faster on sustained CPU/GPU utilization), 4) Canary rollout with rollback policy and fallback to hosted model variants, 5) Cost alerts on token burn rate.
[07:02] Marcus: The canary rollback — how quick is that? If a model regression hits, can we move traffic back to hosted instantly?
[07:10] Raj: You can set automatic fallback policies. There's a small reconfiguration time but it's seconds to minutes depending on routing; for model regression, autoswitch to a validated hosted variant is supported.
[07:25] Priya: For the Dedicated pilot, what baseline capacity should we pick? We want enough headroom for 99th percentile bursts for two weeks.
[07:34] Raj: We'll start with an analysis of your historical peak and synthetic stress test. For two-week headroom, typically 1.5-2x your observed peak steady-state. We'll propose numbers in the SOW.
[08:00] Hannah: Finance asked for a per-model cost forecast next quarter vs hosted.
[08:05] Maya: We'll send a CSV with per-model per-region unit costs and examples of expected monthly bill across several traffic scenarios — optimistic, baseline, pessimistic.
[08:20] Marcus: Any surprises on egress or infra fees?
[08:24] Maya: For Dedicated, network egress will still apply per-cloud; we include that in the forecast. Also for Private on-prem, infra ops is different (one-time infra + support). We'll delineate those lines.
[08:50] Derek: Reliability concerns: we saw a spike last month where some responses doubled latency due to a concurrent training job bump — can Redwood detect noisy neighbors?
[08:59] Raj: In hosted we monitor tail latency and can alert, but noisy neighbor effects are possible. Dedicated isolates you from multi-tenant noise. Additionally, runtime can pin kernels and reserve GPU slices for critical routes to limit interference.
[09:20] Hannah: Let's talk specifics on benchmark run — we want p50/p95/p99 for 128/512/1024 tokens; also throughput QPS at target latency.
[09:30] Raj: We'll run a scenario matrix: tokens x concurrency x model variant. We'll include both cold KV and warm KV cases. Can you share representative request traces?
[09:42] Priya: Yes, we'll export a 72-hour window and remove PII.
[09:47] Raj: Great. For benchmarking we'll use a harness that measures end-to-end latency including network and tokenization. We'll publish a repo and an ephemeral dashboard.
[10:05] Marcus: Rollout timeline — if pilot looks good, how long to full Dedicated?
[10:10] Maya: Depends on procurement but operationally a Dedicated pool can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks once specs and contracts are agreed. Private/VPC adds ~4-8 weeks for networking and KMS integration.
[10:28] Hannah: Procurement will need a clear SOW and a security package.
[10:32] Elena: We'll include a security appendix and sample contractual SLAs with the SOW draft.
[10:45] Derek: Any recommended throttling or guardrails on client side to avoid hitting our own bursts?
[10:50] Raj: Client-side rate limiting, token budget per session, and preemptive batching thresholds recommended. Also backpressure signals from the runtime can be surfaced to clients.
[11:05] Priya: For cost optimization, could we mix models — use a smaller model for classification and big model for longform?
[11:11] Raj: Yes, hybrid routing by intent is effective. Redwood routing policy can direct requests by metadata to different model variants or regions.
[11:25] Hannah: Ok, quick recap?
[11:28] Maya: Recap — Redwood sends cost CSV by model/region, Raj to run benchmark plan, Longview to send traffic traces and SLOs, Elena to draft SOW + security appendix. We'll target benchmark week next week. Share deck: https://redwood.ai/longview/qbr-deck (internal link).
[11:50] Marcus: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[11:53] Priya: Procurement wants price bands and expected commitment level.
[11:56] Maya: We'll include tiered pricing options in the SOW (monthly commit bands).
[12:08] Hannah: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the benchmark.
[12:10] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email w/ artifacts and proposed benchmark times.
[12:15] (call ends)
